title: The Finance Commission

endcard.line: Pictures: Ankur Panchbudhe (CC BY 2.0); Beohar Rammanohar Sinha (public domain)

segments.say: The Centre collects most of India's taxes. The states do most of the spending, on schools, hospitals and police. So who decides how the money is shared?

anim.title: Article 280
items: A Finance Commission every five years

segments.say: The Constitution's answer, in Article two eighty, is a Finance Commission, set up by the President every five years.

anim.title: Its two big jobs
items: Vertical: how much of the tax pool goes to all states
Horizontal: how that share is split between states

segments.say: It has two big jobs. First, how much of the Centre's tax pool goes to the states together. Second, how that share is split among them.

anim.title: States' share of the divisible tax pool

segments.say: The fourteenth Commission raised the states' share to forty-two percent. The fifteenth set it at forty-one, after Jammu and Kashmir became a union territory.
To split it, the Commission uses a formula. Poorer states get more, and so do larger ones, greener ones, and those that brought down population growth.
It also recommends grants for states that still fall short, and for local bodies like panchayats. Its advice isn't binding, but governments almost always follow it.
For GS Two: Article two eighty, sharing tax between Centre and states, and the backbone of India's fiscal federalism.

sources: Constitution of India, Article 280 (Finance Commission: chairman and four members, every fifth year or earlier; distribution of net tax proceeds and grants-in-aid) and Article 275

quiz.q: Which Article provides for the Finance Commission?
quiz.why: Every five years, appointed by the President.

quiz.q: What share did the 15th FC give the states?
Which criterion had the biggest weight in the 15th FC formula?
quiz.why: 45% for income distance: poorer states get more.
